questions.question:
Convert the sentence into Passive Voice:
'The court clerk prepares the daily cause list every evening.'

options.text: The daily cause list was prepared by the court clerk every evening.
The daily cause list is prepared by the court clerk every evening.
The daily cause list is being prepared by the court clerk every evening.
The daily cause list has been prepared by the court clerk every evening.

questions.explanation: Original active sentence Simple Present ('prepares') mein hai. Passive Voice mein tense freeze rehta hai. Naya subject 'The daily cause list' singular noun hai, isliye Simple Present passive formula 'is + V3' lagega: 'is prepared' (B). Option (A) Simple Past ('was prepared') mein tense badal deta hai jo galat hai. Option (C) continuous hai aur Option (D) perfect hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01: Simple Present Passive Formula = Object + is / am / are + V3 + (by + Subject).
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L04

questions.question:
Convert the sentence into Passive Voice:
'The system engineers are upgrading the high court servers.'

options.text: The high court servers are upgraded by the system engineers.
The high court servers were being upgraded by the system engineers.
The high court servers are being upgraded by the system engineers.
The high court servers have been upgraded by the system engineers.

questions.explanation: Active sentence Present Continuous ('are upgrading') mein hai aur naya subject 'The high court servers' plural noun hai. Continuous passive ka rule hai: 'is/am/are + being + V3'. Plural subject hone ki wajah se 'are being upgraded' (C) sahi answer hai. Option (A) mein 'being' gayab hai jisse wo Simple Present ban gaya. Option (B) mein tense past kar diya gaya jo galat hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-02: Present Continuous Passive = Object + is/am/are + being + V3 + (by + Subject).
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L04

questions.question:
Choose the correct Passive Voice form:
'The selection committee has approved the revised recruitment rules.'

options.text: The revised recruitment rules has been approved by the selection committee.
The revised recruitment rules have been approved by the selection committee.
The revised recruitment rules had been approved by the selection committee.
The revised recruitment rules were approved by the selection committee.

questions.explanation: Active sentence Present Perfect ('has approved') mein hai. Naya subject 'The revised recruitment rules' plural noun hai. Isliye passive auxiliary naye subject ke hisaab se plural 'have been' banegi: 'The revised recruitment rules have been approved...' (B). Option (A) mein plural subject ke sath singular 'has' laga kar agreement error ki gayi hai. Option (C) aur (D) mein tense change ho gaya hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-03: Passive auxiliary ka number aur person naye subject ke according decide hota hai: Plural subject + have been + V3.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L04

questions.question:
Convert into Passive Voice:
'The division bench delivered the final verdict yesterday.'

options.text: The final verdict was delivered by the division bench yesterday.
The final verdict had been delivered by the division bench yesterday.
The final verdict is delivered by the division bench yesterday.
The final verdict was being delivered by the division bench yesterday.

questions.explanation: Active sentence Simple Past ('delivered', V2) mein hai aur naya subject 'The final verdict' singular noun hai. Simple Past passive formula: 'was/were + V3'. Singular subject ke sath 'was delivered' (A) bilkul accurate hai. Option (B) Past Perfect ('had been') banata hai jo ki unnecessary tense backshift hai. Option (C) Present tense hai aur (D) continuous hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-04: Simple Past Passive = Object + was / were + V3 + (by + Subject).
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L04

questions.question:
Convert into Passive Voice:
'The cyber cell did not recover the stolen laptops.'

options.text: The stolen laptops were not recovered by the cyber cell.
The stolen laptops did not recovered by the cyber cell.
The stolen laptops had not been recovered by the cyber cell.
The stolen laptops was not recovered by the cyber cell.

questions.explanation: Active sentence Simple Past Negative ('did not recover') mein hai. Passive banate waqt 'did' gayab ho jata hai aur 'was not / were not + V3' lagta hai. Naya subject 'The stolen laptops' plural hai, isliye 'were not recovered' (A) sahi hai. Option (B) mein 'did' copy kar diya gaya jo ungrammatical hai. Option (D) mein plural 'laptops' ke sath singular 'was' lagaya gaya hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-04 & RC-08: Active 'did not + V1' passive mein 'was not / were not + V3' ban jata hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L04

questions.question:
Choose the correct Passive Voice:
'The auditor was scrutinizing the annual accounts.'

options.text: The annual accounts were scrutinized by the auditor.
The annual accounts were being scrutinized by the auditor.
The annual accounts was being scrutinized by the auditor.
The annual accounts had been scrutinized by the auditor.

questions.explanation: Active sentence Past Continuous ('was scrutinizing') mein hai. Naya subject 'The annual accounts' plural noun hai, isliye plural auxiliary 'were' lagegi aur continuous aspect ke liye 'being' aayega: 'were being scrutinized' (B). Option (A) mein 'being' omit kar diya gaya hai. Option (C) mein plural 'accounts' ke sath singular 'was' laga diya gaya hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-05: Past Continuous Passive = Object + was/were + being + V3 + (by + Subject).
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L04

questions.question:
Convert into Passive Voice:
'The municipal authority had sealed the unauthorized godown before noon.'

options.text: The unauthorized godown was sealed by the municipal authority before noon.
The unauthorized godown had been sealed by the municipal authority before noon.
The unauthorized godown has been sealed by the municipal authority before noon.
The unauthorized godown had sealed by the municipal authority before noon.

questions.explanation: Active sentence Past Perfect ('had sealed') mein hai. Past Perfect passive ka universal formula hai: 'had + been + V3'. Isliye 'had been sealed' (B) correct answer hai. Option (A) Simple Past ('was sealed') banata hai. Option (C) Present Perfect banata hai. Option (D) mein 'been' gayab hai jisse wo active hi reh jata hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-06: Past Perfect Passive = Object + had + been + V3 + (by + Subject).
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L04

questions.question:
Convert into Passive Voice:
'The committee will announce the written test results next week.'

options.text: The written test results will be announced by the committee next week.
The written test results will announced by the committee next week.
The written test results would be announced by the committee next week.
The written test results will have been announced by the committee next week.

questions.explanation: Active sentence Simple Future ('will announce') mein hai. Simple Future passive formula: 'will/shall + be + V3'. Isliye 'will be announced' (A) sahi hai. Option (B) mein 'be' gayab hai. Option (C) mein 'will' ko 'would' mein backshift kiya gaya hai jo Narration ka rule hai, Voice ka nahi. Option (D) Future Perfect hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-07: Simple Future Passive = Object + will/shall + be + V3 + (by + Subject).
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L04

questions.question:
Convert into Passive Voice:
'Does the clerk maintain the confidential dispatch register?'

options.text: Did the confidential dispatch register maintained by the clerk?
Is the confidential dispatch register maintained by the clerk?
Was the confidential dispatch register maintained by the clerk?
Does the confidential dispatch register maintained by the clerk?

questions.explanation: Active sentence Simple Present Yes/No question ('Does + S + V1') hai. Passive banate waqt 'Does' hat kar naye singular subject 'the confidential dispatch register' ke mutabiq Simple Present auxiliary 'Is' sentence ke shuru mein aayegi: 'Is + Object + V3 + by Subject?' ➔ 'Is the confidential dispatch register maintained by the clerk?' (B). Option (C) past tense 'Was' use karta hai jo galat hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09: Simple Present Yes/No Interrogative = Is / Am / Are + Object + V3 + (by + Subject)?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L04

questions.question:
Convert into Passive Voice:
'Who drafted this comprehensive arbitration petition?'

options.text: By whom was this comprehensive arbitration petition drafted?
By whom this comprehensive arbitration petition was drafted?
Who was this comprehensive arbitration petition drafted?
By whom had this comprehensive arbitration petition drafted?

questions.explanation: 'Who' se shuru hone wale Simple Past question ka passive 'By whom + was/were + Object + V3?' hota hai. 'By whom' ke turant baad auxiliary 'was' aana zaroori hai (interrogative inversion). Isliye (A) sahi hai. Option (B) mein assertive word order ('By whom this petition was drafted') use kiya gaya hai jo question format mein galat hai. Option (D) mein 'been' gayab hai aur tense had kar diya gaya hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09: 'Who + V2 + Object?' ➔ 'By whom + was/were + Object + V3?'. Inversion mandatory hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L04

questions.question:
Which is the most appropriate Passive Voice construction for:
'Someone has stolen the original court stamp from the registry.'

options.text: The original court stamp has been stolen from the registry by someone.
The original court stamp has been stolen from the registry.
The original court stamp was stolen from the registry by somebody.
The original court stamp had been stolen from the registry.

questions.explanation: Active sentence mein subject indefinite pronoun 'Someone' hai jiska doer unknown hai. Standard formal English aur competitive exams mein jab doer unknown ya vague ho, toh 'by someone' ko naturally omit kar diya jata hai. Isliye (B) grammatically superior aur correct option hai. Option (A) redundant agent rakhta hai, aur (C) wa (D) mein tense distorted hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-10: Indefinite pronouns (someone, somebody, people) ko passive mein 'by + agent' ke roop mein naturally omit kiya jata hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L04

questions.question: Which of the following active sentences CANNOT be converted into Passive Voice?

options.text: The magistrate signed the detention order.
The high court advocates staged a peaceful protest.
The key prosecution witness died in the hospital last night.
The system assistant repaired the network cable.

questions.explanation: Sentence (C) mein verb 'died' purely intransitive verb hai. 'Died' ke baad koi direct object nahi hai ('in the hospital' place adverbial hai, aur 'last night' time adverbial hai). Chunki object nahi hai, isliye iska koi passive transformation possible nahi hai ('The witness was died' kehna gross grammatical blunder hai). Baaki teeno sentences (A, B, D) mein transitive verbs hain jinke paas direct objects ('detention order', 'peaceful protest', 'network cable') hain.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-10 & Section H: Strictly transitive verbs hi passive voice form karti hain. Purely intransitive verbs (die, sleep, arrive, go, laugh) ka passive voice nahi banta.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L04
